newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will appear before a House Banking subcommittee on July 22 as part of his semiannual "Humphrey-Hawkins" testimony on monetary policy and economic conditions, a Congressional source said on Monday.
The hearings will include a second day of testimony from private sector economists and a discussion of current Fed monetary policy options.
House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach agreed to schedule the extra session in April in response to a request signed by 21 of 24 Democrats on the House Banking Committee.
Many Democrats, as well as Republicans, waged an active public campaign to convince Fed officials to hold interest rates steady at the last Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.
The FOMC voted to raise the federal funds rate to 5.5 percent from 5.25 percent at its March 25 meeting. It next convenes on July 1-2.
The Senate Banking Committee, which takes turns leading the Humphrey-Hawkins hearings with its House counterpart, has yet to schedule its own session.
